About J3D.AI

An advisory and technology company built on the conviction that collaboration should be more profitable than competition.

The Company

J3D.AI (JED-EYE)

J3D.AI is an advisory and technology company headquartered in Tallinn, Estonia. We deliver market access advisory, AI readiness scoring and implementation, and sovereign convening for organizations navigating the AI transition across Europe and Asia.

Founded on the principle that peace must become more profitable than war - and that collaboration, structured correctly, creates more value than competition. This shapes every engagement: who is in the room, how dialogue is structured, and what outcomes are measured.

“We exist to make peace more profitable than war - and collaboration more profitable than competition.”

Yip Thy-Diep Ta - CEO, J3D.AI

Who We Work With

Governments, capital, and founders.

We work with sovereign governments and ministries navigating AI policy and trade corridors, capital allocators seeking intelligence on emerging markets and technology transitions, and deep-tech founders building at the intersection of AI, governance, and resilience. The common thread: organizations where the decisions being made are consequential.

Overview

Better Together: Cross-Border Collaborations for Resilient Economies

House of Collaboration is J3D.AI's flagship sovereign convening platform - an invitation-only side event during WEF week in Davos. Founded by Yip Thy-Diep Ta and Kevin Varend, the third edition in January 2026 was anchored by the theme "Better Together: Cross-Border Collaborations for Resilient Economies."

HoC 2026 convened 860 senior leaders from 70+ countries representing €3 trillion in GDP. The edition launched first-of-kind sub-platforms inside the umbrella: Estonian Leap, the New Nordics Ministerial Innovation Reception, the J3D.AI Hydrogen Roundtable, and the launch of Futures Beyond Our Time with the Bavarian Foresight Institute.

The Challenge

High-Stakes Diplomacy at Scale

Build the one convening at Davos that the world's top decision-makers feel they cannot skip - and convert that gravity into measurable partnerships, capital deployment, and policy outcomes.

1

Constant Agenda Changes

High-level speakers confirm, cancel, and reschedule constantly. A session announced Monday might have a different speaker by Wednesday.

2

Rigorous Vetting at Scale

Every delegate vetted before invitation. 860+ applicants required a multi-stage HubSpot CRM workflow.

3

Sub-Platform Editorial Integrity

Estonian Leap, Hydrogen Roundtable, Foresight whitepaper launch - each had to feel like a flagship in its own right under one umbrella.

The Solution

Six-Layer PPP Model, One Editorial Umbrella

1

Invitation-Only Architecture

Sovereign curation, not paid access. Every delegate vetted through HubSpot.

2

Six-Layer PPP Model

Policy Anchor · Industry Infrastructure · Startup Layer · Multilateral Legitimacy · Capital Layer · Physical Execution.

3

Integrated Intelligence Stack

J3D.AI Conference Intelligence deployed live - report-ready outputs with 95% noise elimination.

4

Tier-1 Media Discipline

Orchestrated coverage in The Washington Post, Blick (~90M monthly), CGTN, MFA Estonia, regional press.

Overview

Sovereign Cloud, Autonomous Mobility, AI Upskilling of a Nation

Estonian Leap is the first dedicated country-level day at Davos inside the House of Collaboration umbrella. Co-produced with the Estonian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) and the Estonian Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications (MKM), the inaugural Estonian Leap day ran on Tuesday January 20, 2026 as a flagship sub-platform of HoC 2026.

The thesis: a small, governance-disciplined nation does not need to lease a country house at Davos. It can embed into a sovereign-grade convening and outperform full pavilions - on signal, partnerships, and media. Estonian Leap did exactly that.

The Challenge

Country Presence at Davos, Without a Country House

A nation of 1.3 million has limited fixed-cost budget for a standalone Davos pavilion. Estonia needed a model that delivered the visibility of a country house with the editorial discipline of a curated convening.

1

Pavilion-Level Visibility, Sub-Platform Footprint

Deliver the media and partnership outcomes of a country house without leasing one. Inside HoC, not next to it.

2

Ministerial Choreography

Four ministerial appearances coordinated with parallel diplomatic schedules during the busiest week of the year.

3

Three Distinct Thematic Pillars in One Day

Sovereign Cloud, Autonomous Mobility, and AI Upskilling of a Nation - each substantial enough to anchor its own session.

The Solution

Sub-Platform Architecture Inside HoC

1

Embedded, Not Adjacent

Estonian Leap ran inside the House of Collaboration umbrella, sharing the HoC media stack, intelligence platform, and delegate pool.

2

Three-Pillar Programming

Sovereign Cloud · Autonomous Mobility · AI Upskilling of a Nation. Each pillar with confirmed ministerial and corporate anchors.

3

Co-Produced with MFA + MKM

Two Estonian ministries as direct co-producers - ensuring policy authority and sovereign-grade protocol throughout.

4

Tier-1 Media Anchoring

Coverage secured in MFA Estonia channels, Ringvaade (Estonian national press), Blick, and integrated into HoC's Washington Post + CGTN footprint.

Overview

A Castle, a Thesis, a Durable Community

The J3D.AI Deep Tech Castle is a 4-day immersive retreat in an 18th-century castle in central Germany - designed to convene 100 founders, investors, scientists, and operators around a deliberate thesis: Zebracorns, technically ambitious and socially responsible ventures shaping a better future.

The 2025 edition ran from June 26–29 at Schloss Burgscheidungen with five tracks (AI, Web3, Sustainability, Longevity, Health). Residential capacity of 31–56 beds anchors the inner core; daytime visitors expand to 100. The format deliberately rejects the conference-stage attention economy.

The Challenge

Build the European Retreat the Conference Circuit Cannot

Unicorns optimise for valuation. Zebracorns optimise for impact and durability. Europe's deep-tech ecosystem needed a convening built around that thesis - with operational discipline, not just atmosphere.

1

Castle as Operating Venue

Operating a centuries-old castle as a fully staffed retreat - kitchens, sleeping logistics, AV, security, transport across 4 days.

2

Residential vs Daytime Balance

31–56 residential beds balanced with 100 daytime cohort, sequenced so the experience does not feel two-tier.

3

Five Disparate Tracks, One Voice

30+ programmed hours across AI, Web3, Sustainability, Longevity, Health without losing the Zebracorn editorial thesis.

The Solution

Atmosphere as a Feature, Not Decoration

1

Zebracorn Editorial Thesis

Ambition + responsibility, encoded into every applicant's curation funnel. Track leads enforce the framing.

2

MOPS Operating Framework

Marketing / Operations / Programming / Sales with explicit RACI per function. Programme booked ≥2 weeks before event.

3

Persistent Post-Event Asset

Castle Retreat Magazine on Yumpu becomes a long-tail discovery and credibility tool - not a one-off PDF.

4

Five-Track Programme

AI · Web3 · Sustainability · Longevity · Health - each curated by a dedicated track lead.

Overview

Technology, Philosophy, Ethics, Governance - in One Room

SyntAIgration: Thinking Beyond Cyber was a 3-day intervention at ESMT Berlin's Digital Society Institute (DSI) - convening 32 international thought leaders across cybersecurity, AI, philosophy & ethics, and public-private governance. Co-hosted with Allianz, Deloitte, Palo Alto Networks, Malik.

The opening question: "How can we shape the current technological disruption, anticipate future developments, and best collaborate to adapt as a society - and achieve a zero-exclusion world worth living for everyone?" The format directly informed the design of the Allianz NextGenIT Think Tank and the editorial discipline that now anchors every J3D.AI Platform engagement.

32
Thought leaders

Overview

A 100-Year Horizon, Taken Seriously

Futures Beyond Our Time - Our World in 2125 is a foresight whitepaper co-authored by 42 global experts, co-produced by J3D.AI Labs and the Bavarian Foresight Institute. The research emerged from foresight workshops at the House of Collaboration in Davos in early 2025, was published under embargoed launch on July 21, 2025, and held an in-person Munich launch in September 2025.

A bold question anchored the project: What might the world look like in 2125? Forty-two authors from across generations, geographies, and disciplines mapped imaginative-yet-plausible futures across nine thematic dimensions.

Who the House is for

Six seats at the table.

The House is invitation-only. Most delegations recognise themselves in one of six archetypes - find yours, then start the conversation.

The Established Brand
A recognised company with real market standing, looking to shape a narrative and engage the right stakeholders.
The National Government or Agency
A ministry, agency or national innovation body seeking dialogue with investors and institutional leaders.
The Deep-Tech Scale-Up
A scale-up with serious momentum and unicorn potential, positioning as a category leader - not just visibility.
The Research & Innovation Platform
A think tank, research institute or university seeking visibility for ideas and partnerships.
The Institutional Mission-Driven Actor
An established NGO, foundation or multilateral that belongs in serious cross-sector dialogue.
The Proven Capital Allocator
A respected fund or allocator with a real track record that wants curated access - not fundraising theatre.

FAQ

Questions delegates ask.

How exclusive is the House of Collaboration?

Invitation-only. Every delegate is vetted. Around 850 senior leaders take part in each edition.

Do you have partnership pricing?

Yes - Entry, Mid and High tiers. Request the prospectus or book a call and we’ll match you to the right one.

What’s included in each tier?

Entry = brand presence + ROI report. Mid = Entry + active participation + curated matchmaking. High = Mid + full strategic partnership + agenda-driven access.

Can I send a deputy?

In limited circumstances. Cohort integrity is core to the format, so we keep substitutions to a minimum.

Are sessions confidential?

Yes. The Chatham House Rule applies inside all closed sessions.

How is HoC different from a typical Davos event?

Decision density over audience size. Curated invitation, not paid access. Long-term capital and policy deployment, not short-term deal flow.

When are sector-exclusive allocations confirmed?

On a rolling basis. Sectors close as commitments come in, so earlier conversations have more room.

How do I apply?

Apply via the Airtable form, or book a 30-minute partnership call.

Archive - HoC 2025 Edition

Davos 2025 - Peace as Policy.

The second edition of the House of Collaboration. 150 delegates. Foresight as practice. Technology with purpose.

2025 Theme

Peace as Policy. Foresight as Practice. Technology with Purpose.

The 2025 edition convened 150 delegates from across the world during Davos week. The week was anchored on three propositions: that peace is a policy choice, foresight is a practice rather than a forecast, and technology serves human ends or it serves none.

Highlights included the launch of the Foresight Whitepaper (42 experts, 9 visions of the future), the inaugural Estonian Leap programme, and the first Peace Gala Dinner during Davos week.

programme architecture

A Sovereign PPP Execution Platform.
Not a Side Event.

Estonian Leap is co-produced with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Estonia and the Ministry of Economic Affairs & Communications. A replicable architecture for sovereign public-private partnership at Davos - designed for outcomes, not optics.

It demonstrates what country-level PPP execution looks like when designed for economic development rather than visibility: investment flows, bilateral partnerships, MoU pipelines, and technology adoption across emerging markets.

Publication · 2025

Inside Davos Foresight Whitepaper - Our World in 2125.

42 global experts. 9 visions of the future. In partnership with the Bavarian Foresight Institute. Distributed at HoC Davos 2025.

Methodology

Foresight as practice, not prediction.

The Foresight Whitepaper is a structured contribution from 42 global experts - founders, scientists, policymakers, philosophers and capital allocators - each providing a sectoral 100-year forecast under shared methodological constraints. The result is nine plausible visions of our world in 2125, grouped across thematic clusters.

Co-developed with the Bavarian Foresight Institute, the document was distributed in print at HoC Davos 2025 to heads of state, sovereign wealth funds, and senior multilateral leaders.

9 Themes

The thematic clusters.

01 · Climate & Planetary Boundaries

Habitability, biosphere recovery, and the cost of inaction.

02 · AI & Cognition

Foundation models, agentic systems, and the future of human cognition.

03 · Multipolar Geopolitics

A world without a hegemon - what governance becomes.

04 · Health & Longevity

Brain capital, biotech, and what it means to age in 2125.

05 · Energy Transition

Fusion, storage, and the geography of post-carbon power.

06 · Capital & Markets

What investing looks like when planning horizons exceed lifetimes.

07 · Education & Knowledge

From schools to lifelong cognitive infrastructure.

08 · Cities & Mobility

Megacities, planetary mobility, and the ground beneath our feet.

09 · Peace & Cooperation

Whether peace becomes more profitable than conflict.

Privacy Policy

GDPR-compliant disclosure of how J3D.AI Labs OÜ collects, processes, and stores personal data.

Last updated: May 2026 · Compliant with EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) (EU) 2016/679 and Estonian Personal Data Protection Act.

Contents
  1. Controller & contact
  2. Data we collect
  3. Legal basis for processing
  4. Cookies & tracking technologies
  5. Third-party processors
  6. Your rights as a data subject
  7. Data retention
  8. International transfers
  9. Children & minors
  10. Changes & complaints

1. Data Controller

The controller responsible for the processing of personal data on j3d.ai is:

J3D.AI Labs OÜ
Tallinn, Estonia
Email: primary@j3d.ai

2. Data We Collect

2.1 Data you provide directly

  • Contact data submitted via forms (name, email, organisation, message content)
  • Calendar booking data submitted through Calendly (name, email, scheduled time, optional context provided in intake questions)
  • Event applications and delegate registration data (job title, country, sector, declared interests)
  • Email correspondence with our team

2.2 Data collected automatically

  • Server logs (IP address, browser, referrer, pages visited, timestamps) - retained for security and abuse prevention
  • Analytics data (anonymised page views, session duration, navigation flow) via privacy-respecting tools
  • Cookies as described in section 4

3. Legal Basis for Processing

We process personal data on the following GDPR Article 6 bases:

  • Consent (Art. 6(1)(a)) - for marketing communications, optional cookies, newsletter sign-ups
  • Contractual necessity (Art. 6(1)(b)) - for event participation, advisory engagements, service delivery
  • Legitimate interests (Art. 6(1)(f)) - for security logging, fraud prevention, and improvement of our services where these interests are not overridden by your fundamental rights
  • Legal obligation (Art. 6(1)(c)) - for invoicing, tax records, and statutory retention

4. Cookies & Tracking

We use the following categories of cookies and tracking technologies:

  • Strictly necessary - session management, security, form submission. No consent required.
  • Analytics - aggregate visitor behaviour to improve content. We use Google Analytics 4 in IP-anonymised mode with Consent Mode v2. Loaded only after consent.
  • Marketing - HubSpot tracking pixel for lead attribution and campaign measurement. Loaded only after consent.

You may withdraw consent at any time via the cookie banner or by emailing primary@j3d.ai. Refusing non-essential cookies will not impair your access to the site.

5. Third-Party Processors

We engage the following processors under GDPR Art. 28 data processing agreements:

  • Vercel Inc. - web hosting and edge delivery (US, with EU regions where available)
  • HubSpot Ireland Limited - CRM, forms, marketing automation (EU data centre)
  • Calendly LLC - meeting booking (US, SCCs in place)
  • Google LLC - Workspace email and analytics (EU data residency where available)
  • Microsoft Azure - legacy hosting for davos.j3d.ai archive (EU region)

6. Your Rights

Under GDPR, you have the following rights regarding your personal data:

  • Right of access (Art. 15) - obtain a copy of your data
  • Right to rectification (Art. 16) - correct inaccurate data
  • Right to erasure / “right to be forgotten” (Art. 17)
  • Right to restriction of processing (Art. 18)
  • Right to data portability (Art. 20)
  • Right to object (Art. 21) - in particular against direct marketing
  • Right to withdraw consent at any time, without affecting prior lawful processing
  • Right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority (in Estonia: Andmekaitse Inspektsioon)

To exercise any of these rights, email primary@j3d.ai. We respond within 30 days.

7. Data Retention

  • Contact form submissions: 24 months from last interaction
  • Event registration data: 36 months post-event for impact reporting and alumni programmes
  • Invoicing and accounting records: 7 years (Estonian statutory requirement)
  • Server logs: 90 days
  • Marketing consent records: until withdrawn or 24 months of inactivity

8. International Transfers

Where personal data is transferred outside the EEA (e.g. to US-based processors), we rely on EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and verify supplementary measures where required by the Schrems II decision.

9. Children

Our services are not directed to individuals under the age of 18. We do not knowingly collect personal data from minors. If you believe we have inadvertently done so, please contact us for immediate deletion.

10. Changes & Complaints

We may update this policy to reflect operational, legal, or regulatory changes. Material changes will be communicated via the website and, where appropriate, by email. The version date at the top of this page reflects the most recent update.

If you have a concern that we have not resolved, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the Estonian Data Protection Inspectorate (www.aki.ee) or your local EU supervisory authority.

Legal · Events

House of Collaboration - Terms & Policy

Booking conditions, code of conduct, and event-specific policies for all HoC programmes.

Last updated: May 2026 · These terms apply to all House of Collaboration events operated by J3D.AI Labs OÜ including HoC Davos, Estonian Leap, and Deep Tech Castle.

1. Booking & Registration

All delegate registrations are subject to review and approval by J3D.AI Labs OÜ. Submission of an application does not guarantee a delegate pass. Successful applicants will receive written confirmation within 5 business days. J3D.AI reserves the right to decline any application without providing a reason.

2. Payment Terms

Full payment is required within 14 days of invoice issuance. Delegate passes are non-transferable unless written consent is provided by J3D.AI. VAT will be applied where applicable under Estonian and EU tax law.

3. Cancellation & Refund Policy

  • More than 60 days before the event: 100% refund minus a 10% administration fee.
  • 31-60 days before the event: 50% refund.
  • 30 days or fewer before the event: No refund. Transfer to a future edition may be offered at J3D.AI’s discretion.
  • Event cancellation by J3D.AI: Full refund of amounts paid.

4. Code of Conduct

All delegates, speakers, sponsors, and staff are required to maintain the highest standards of professional conduct. J3D.AI events operate under the Chatham House Rule unless explicitly stated otherwise. Discrimination, harassment, or disruptive behaviour will result in immediate removal without refund.

All sessions are off-the-record unless the relevant speaker or session leader explicitly grants permission for attribution. Photography and video recording are subject to session-specific rules communicated on-site.

5. Programme Changes

J3D.AI reserves the right to modify the programme, venue, speakers, or format at any time. Every effort will be made to communicate material changes in advance. Delegate fees are not refundable due to speaker or session changes.

6. Liability

J3D.AI Labs OÜ accepts no liability for loss of property, personal injury, or consequential losses arising from attendance at or travel to any J3D.AI event. Delegates are responsible for arranging appropriate travel and health insurance.

7. Data Protection

Delegate registration data is processed in accordance with our Privacy Policy. By registering, delegates consent to their name and organisation being listed in the delegate directory shared with other confirmed delegates, unless they opt out at the time of registration.

8. Governing Law

These terms are governed by Estonian law. Any disputes shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Estonian courts.

For all event-related enquiries: primary@j3d.ai

Research & Practice

J3D.AI Fellows.

A curated cohort of practitioners, researchers, and policymakers who contribute to and shape the intellectual output of J3D.AI.

What is a J3D.AI Fellow?

Practitioners who help shape the rooms.

J3D.AI Fellows are distinguished practitioners, researchers, and policymakers who contribute to J3D.AI’s intellectual outputs and convening programmes. Fellowship is by invitation, extended to individuals whose work sits at the intersection of AI governance, technology, capital, and public policy.

Fellows participate in shaping the agenda at the House of Collaboration, contribute to J3D.AI research publications, and have access to the J3D.AI Members Portal and intelligence archives.
